tagline: Down the Whitewater valley beside a canal that fell too fast.
intro: The byway starts at Hagerstown, the canal's northern end, and follows the Whitewater River down its valley through Cambridge City, Connersville, Laurel, Metamora and Brookville toward Lawrenceburg on the Ohio. It keeps to the line of a canal that dropped 491 feet in 76 miles, 6.4 feet to the mile, nearly four times the grade of the Erie.

It took 56 locks and seven dams to manage that, and the steepness was trouble whenever heavy rains came. Indiana went bankrupt in 1839 and the work stopped until 1842, and in November 1847 a flood washed out long stretches, a few months after the last of the canal reached Hagerstown.

moments.title: Cambridge City
moments.text: The canal reached this National Road town in 1846, and the town still keeps Canal Days on the second weekend of every September.

moments.title: Laurel
moments.text: James Conwell of Maryland platted the town in 1836 and nearly named it New Baltimore. Canal boats were arriving by 1843.

moments.title: Metamora
moments.text: Canal water still turns the restored grain mill here and crosses Duck Creek on a wooden aqueduct, a reconstruction of the one built in 1846.
